reviewer: Codex research agent, delegated researcher and verifier
scope: Five individually researched profiles with official burial evidence. This is not approval of the national candidate queue. No photos included. Coordinates are cemetery or campus reference points, not surveyed graves. Herbert Hoover is excluded pending reconciliation of the imported library entity with his actual NPS hillside gravesite.

candidates.name: William Howard Taft
candidates.short_description: 27th U.S. president and the only president to also serve as chief justice of the Supreme Court.
candidates.biography: William Howard Taft served as the 27th U.S. president and later as chief justice of the Supreme Court, the only person to hold both offices. Before reaching the White House, the Cincinnati native worked as a judge, governor-general of the Philippines, and secretary of war. He is buried in Section 30 of Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: Taft reached the highest office in both the executive and judicial branches of the U.S. government.

burial_evidence.notes: Arlington's dedicated gravesite page explicitly confirms actual burial in Section 30, despite Memorial Grave in its title. NPS's biography independently confirms full dates, identity, cemetery, presidency, and judicial career. Presidents, politics, and history tags reflect those documented roles; civilian Secretary of War service is not grounds for a military tag. Local QID and Wikipedia article match the official biography. Imported cemetery reference point only, not the grave or visitor entrance.

candidates.name: John F. Kennedy
candidates.short_description: 35th U.S. president and decorated World War II Navy veteran whose Arlington gravesite is marked by an eternal flame.
candidates.biography: John F. Kennedy was the 35th U.S. president. A decorated Navy veteran of World War II, he represented Massachusetts in Congress before winning the 1960 presidential election. His presidency ended with his assassination in Dallas in 1963. An eternal flame marks his gravesite at Arlington National Cemetery.
candidates.why_interesting: Before becoming president, Kennedy commanded PT-109 and helped his crew survive its sinking in the South Pacific.

burial_evidence.notes: Arlington confirms actual interment and the permanent eternal-flame gravesite, distinct from the original temporary plot within the same cemetery. JFK Library's biography supports presidency, congressional career, and decorated Navy service, supporting presidents, politics, military, and history tags. Its Fast Facts page confirms exact birth and death dates: https://www.jfklibrary.org/learn/about-jfk/life-of-john-f-kennedy/fast-facts-john-f-kennedy. Local QID and article identity match. Imported cemetery point is not an exact flame/grave coordinate.

candidates.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
candidates.burial_place_name: Dwight D. Eisenhower Presidential Library, Museum and Boyhood Home
candidates.short_description: 34th U.S. president and Allied commander during the Normandy invasion.
candidates.biography: Dwight D. Eisenhower commanded Allied forces during the Normandy invasion before serving two terms as U.S. president. His administration authorized the Interstate Highway System and established NASA. He is buried in the Place of Meditation on the grounds of his presidential library in Abilene, Kansas, alongside Mamie Eisenhower and their son Doud Dwight.
candidates.why_interesting: His career connected the command of the D-Day invasion with the creation of America's Interstate Highway System.

burial_evidence.notes: The National Archives presidential library gives exact dates and explicitly confirms burial in the Place of Meditation on its Abilene campus on April 2, 1969. It identifies the building as the final resting place of Dwight, Mamie, and Doud Dwight. The separate official chronology confirms identity, Normandy command, presidential terms, Interstate Highway System, and NASA; these support presidents, politics, military, and history tags. Local QID and article identity match. Campus reference coordinate only; the grave is inside the Place of Meditation, not the museum exhibit area.

candidates.name: Harry S. Truman
candidates.burial_place_name: Harry S. Truman Presidential Library and Museum
candidates.short_description: 33rd U.S. president and World War I artillery officer, buried in his presidential library's courtyard.
candidates.biography: Harry S. Truman became the 33rd U.S. president after Franklin Roosevelt's death in 1945. A Missouri farmer and World War I artillery officer before entering national politics, he later won the closely watched 1948 election. His administration introduced the Marshall Plan and ordered desegregation of the armed forces. Harry and Bess Truman are buried in their presidential library's courtyard.
candidates.why_interesting: His path to the presidency ran through farming, a clothing store, wartime artillery command, and Missouri politics.

burial_evidence.notes: The National Archives library history explicitly confirms President and Mrs. Truman are buried in its Independence courtyard. The official biographical sketch independently confirms exact dates, burial, presidency, World War I artillery command, and the other biography details. These support presidents, politics, military, and history tags. His county judge office was administrative, not judicial; no judicial role is inferred. Local QID and article identity match. Library campus reference coordinate only, not a surveyed courtyard grave pin.

candidates.name: Ronald Reagan
candidates.short_description: U.S. president, California governor, and actor whose earlier career included radio and Army training films.
candidates.biography: Ronald Reagan worked as a radio announcer and film actor before becoming governor of California and president of the United States. His earlier career included leading the Screen Actors Guild and making Army training films during World War II. He is buried beside Nancy Reagan at the presidential library in Simi Valley, at a site he selected overlooking the surrounding valley.
candidates.why_interesting: His career moved from recreating baseball games on radio to Hollywood, California politics, and the White House.

burial_evidence.notes: The library's supporting foundation explicitly confirms June 11, 2004 interment on the western campus and Nancy's burial beside him. The National Archives library's pre-presidential timeline confirms birth, acting, broadcasting, governorship, and active Army service in training-film production, supporting entertainment, politics, military, and history; this was not combat service and sports broadcasting is not a sports-star career. Presidency and June 5, 2004 death are also documented at https://www.reaganlibrary.gov/reagans/ronald-reagan/reagan-post-presidency-chronology. Local QID and article identity match. Library campus reference coordinate only, not exact grave precision. No foundation images reused.
